comment: Licenses the shipped app may contain without a second look: permissive ones plus MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft). WeebSync itself is AGPL-3.0-only, so copyleft that is compatible with it (LGPL, GPL-2.0-or-later) is not forbidden, but it is never allowed in bulk: each such package is listed under exceptions with its exact license string and the reason. A changed license string fails the check again. Checked by frontend/scripts/licenses.mjs check, run from tools/licenses/generate.sh and CI.

jassub.license: LGPL-2.1-or-later AND (FTL OR GPL-2.0-or-later) AND MIT AND MIT-Modern-Variant AND ISC AND NTP AND Zlib AND BSL-1.0
jassub.why: The subtitle renderer: libass and the libraries it builds on, compiled to WebAssembly and shipped unmodified from the npm package. Its LGPL-2.1-or-later part is compatible with the AGPL-3.0 app, whose complete source is published anyway; FreeType is taken under FTL.

FriBidi (in jassub's WebAssembly).why: The bidirectional text algorithm libass uses, linked into jassub's WebAssembly (listed from tools/licenses/npm-overrides.json). LGPL-2.1-or-later is compatible with the AGPL-3.0 app, whose complete source is published; its full text ships with the entry.

rvfc-polyfill.why: A requestVideoFrameCallback polyfill pulled in by jassub. Section 13 of both the GPL-3.0 and the AGPL-3.0 explicitly permits combining a GPL-3.0 work with an AGPL-3.0 work; the combination is conveyed under the AGPL-3.0 with the polyfill's own terms kept for its part.
